column1: # Book 5 review (Fable, 2026-10-30). No findings. 5.196 and 5.198-199 conformed to the Book 2 review text (2.178, 2.180-181; paratam = prepared, rerum = things where the Latin differs); 5.195 keeps "But" for the paragraph-opening Quod si. 5.210-212 parallel to 1.211-212 (cimus ad ortus = rouse them to birth). 5.224 "the shores of light": the Latin has no dias, as at 2.577. 5.184: drafting note removed (principia = beginnings is in the register). 5.186 species creandi = a likeness of creation. aetherius sol = the sun in the ether (5.215, 5.267, 5.389). 5.146, 5.160, 5.180, 5.190, 5.192-194, 5.222, 5.229, 5.231 brought into the band; 5.193 lengthened.

column2: Again, you cannot possibly believe that the holy
and that it is sin that what, by the gods' ancient reasoning,
was founded for the races of men to last through endless age,
and was never counted, what harm is it not to have been created?
or in what way was the power of the beginnings ever known,
if nature herself did not give a likeness of creation?
and to meet in every way and to try out all things
so it is no wonder if they fell into such arrangements
and come, as well, into such courses
as those by which this sum of things is now carried on by renewal.
this, still, from the very order of heaven I would dare
that by no means for us, by divine power, was prepared
the nature of things: so great the flaws it stands endowed with.
If we did not, turning the fertile clods with the plowshare
and working the soil of the earth, rouse them to birth,
either the sun in the ether scorches them with too much heat,
